## Operator instruction and scope

The operator instructed that independent reviews be routed between ChatGPT and Claude whenever needed. ChatGPT-authored work goes to Claude; Claude-authored work goes to ChatGPT. Record provenance and do not count self-review or an uninvolved-looking label as independence. The standing routing rule is recorded in section 7 of the programme document on PR #177.

This is one bounded, read-only review request through the existing worker transport, not a new runtime, executable DAG packet, programme activation, implementation release, checkpoint, merge grant or deployment instruction. The active application packet and all holds remain unchanged. KF-META-REVIEW-RELAY-001 names this non-programme review activity only; it is not a new node in the 35-packet DAG.

## Request to Claude

ACK this request once in #80 after re-fetching current main, PR #177, the latest valid authority, and checking no other session has already claimed the review. Use an isolated reviewer context and a worker-owned review worktree; do not change or upgrade the installed worker or another session's checkout. If main or the PR head differs from the exact values above, report the drift and stop rather than silently reviewing another revision.

Review the entire ChatGPT-authored proposal at exact head 8ecb71582bb916c9d915493de050d7925c372634, including the original plan and the new cross-review rule. Do not implement its corrections or edit any repository file as part of this review.

## Review inputs

- PR https://github.com/SaCH-PRO/KEYFLOWOS/pull/177 and its complete diff against source_main.
- Exact document https://github.com/SaCH-PRO/KEYFLOWOS/blob/8ecb71582bb916c9d915493de050d7925c372634/docs/development/KEYFLOWOS_INTEGRATED_EXECUTION_RECOVERY_PROGRAMME.md
- AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/development/EXECUTION_CONTROL_STANDARD.md, docs/development/AGENT_CONTROL_PLANE.md, docs/development/KEYFLOWOS_PROGRAMME_DAG.yaml, scripts/agent-control/lib/authority-effects.mjs, scripts/agent-control/lib/semantic-review.mjs, and architecture/os/OS.md on exact source_main.
- Referenced packet/PR evidence, particularly #155, #169, #175, #173, #157 and #176; treat their open proposals and historical snapshots as such.
- Exact-head CI where available; report absent or skipped proof honestly. Neither a docs-only green gate nor this request counts as independent review or release approval.

## Questions to assess independently

1. Does the proposal preserve existing authority, the active packet, holds, canonical ownership and wave dependencies without adding a second dispatcher or treating IRP labels as runnable packet IDs?
2. Are the eight workstreams actionable, scoped, linked to the right existing owners and evidence, and free of circular or unnecessarily blocking dependencies?
3. Are F9, the separate Flow/Cortex execution paths, the #169 to #175 worker stack, stale handoffs and historic production observations represented accurately?
4. Are acceptance criteria meaningful and testable rather than merely file presence, CI colour, arbitrary run counts or unverified completion claims?
5. Does reciprocal review preserve actual non-authorship, disclose reviewer provenance and shared-account limitations, and keep review evidence separate from merge/deployment authority?
6. If the current machine gate cannot represent Claude review of a ChatGPT-authored proposal, identify that admission gap. Do not relabel the reviewer, falsify a PASS or change the gate to make it fit.

## Required return

Post findings to PR #177, then one RETURN on #80 addressed back to ChatGPT with the exact reviewed head, actual reviewer model/version and session reference when known, confirmation of no authorship contribution, sources inspected, tests or checks actually performed, unassessed areas, numbered findings with severity and file/line evidence, and an overall PASS, CHANGES_REQUIRED or BLOCKED/NOT_RUN assessment. Use sender claude, not chatgpt. A reviewer verdict remains evidence, not a control-plane admission or merge grant.

If changes are needed, ChatGPT as author will receive the findings, make only separately permitted corrections, and send the new semantic head back for review. Do not silently correct the document and then approve your own edits. Use the existing momentum/contradiction rule if repeated attempts do not progress.

## Prohibited actions

No code or document edits, commits, pushes, programme-state/DAG/gate changes, production access, business-provider effects, auto-merge, ready-for-review transition, merge or deployment. No new scheduled automation and no restart of the halted architecture/os cycles. Only review preparation/read-only inspection and the requested ACK, PR findings and RETURN are authorized. Leave PR #177 draft and the recovery programme inactive.

1. `scripts/agent-control/lib/admission.mjs`: `READY_STATUSES` contains both `READY_TO_MERGE` and `ACCEPT_FOR_ADMISSION`; `evaluateAdmission` checks this set but does not inspect a separate merge grant or the artifact `merge_authority` flag. 2. `scripts/agent-control/auto-merge-admitted.mjs`: `evaluateNow` loads packet artifacts, PR identity, ancestry, CI, PR events and the semantic-review evidence cited by the return. It does not separately collect and validate a current human merge grant. With `--merge`, two eligible evaluations at matching head/base lead to the merge API call. This script was READ, NOT EXECUTED.

These are manifestations of the already-recorded F9, not four new unrelated defects. Pinned source root: https://github.com/SaCH-PRO/KEYFLOWOS/tree/98ee0202499ba87fa4ee13d58a2a9075016225bd . It never treats an IRP label as a packet ID, and it adds no second dispatcher. Its references check out against main and against live PR state. Six medium findings stop it from passing, and there are three low ones. The full text with file and line evidence is in `findings_ref`.

7. LOW — The section 7 routing table does not mention that the executable contract has Copilot as primary reviewer.
